What is a random variable?: What is the difference between discrete and continuous data?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Discrete data takes countable values; continuous data can take any value in an interval.

What is a random variable?: What is the mean of a discrete random variable?
A variable that takes numerical values d: E(X) = Σ xP(X=x).

What is a random variable?: What is the variance of a random variable?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]².
The square root of the variance.
A table or function listing all possible values and their probabilities.

What is a random variable?: What must probabilities in a distribution sum to?
What is the binomial distribution used for?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Modelling number of successes in fixed independent trials with constant probability.

What is a random variable?: What are the conditions for a binomial model?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Fixed n, independent trials, two outcomes, constant probability p.

What is a random variable?: What is the mean of a binomial distribution?
A variable that takes numerical values d: np.

What is a random variable?: What is the variance of a binomial distribution?
When can a binomial be approximated by a normal distribution?
A variable that takes numerical values d: When np ≥ 5 and n(1−p) ≥ 5.

What is a random variable?: What is the Poisson distribution used for?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Modelling number of events in fixed interval with constant rate.

What is a random variable?: What is the mean and variance of a Poisson distribution?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Both equal to λ.

What is a random variable?: When can binomial be approximated by Poisson?
A variable that takes numerical values d: When n is large and p is small.
A continuous symmetric bell-shaped distribution defined by mean and variance.

What is a random variable?: What is the standard normal distribution?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Normal distribution with mean 0 and variance 1.
Number of standard deviations a value is from the mean.
Adjusting discrete values by ±0.5 when using normal approximation.

What is a random variable?: What is the Central Limit Theorem?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Sample mean becomes approximately normal as sample size increases.

What is a random variable?: What is the mean of the sampling distribution of the mean?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Equal to population mean.

What is a random variable?: What is the variance of the sampling distribution of the mean?
A variable that takes numerical values d: σ²/n.
Using sample data to test a claim about a population parameter.
The assumption being tested, usually a statement of equality.
The competing claim against H0.
Set of values leading to rejection of H0.
Probability of rejecting H0 when it is true (Type I error rate).

What is a random variable?: What is a Type I error?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Rejecting a true null hypothesis.

What is a random variable?: What is a Type II error?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Failing to reject a false null hypothesis.
Probability of observing result at least as extreme assuming H0 is true.
Measure of strength and direction of linear relationship.

What is a random variable?: What is Pearson's product-moment correlation coefficient?
A variable that takes numerical values d: A measure of linear correlation between −1 and 1.
No linear correlation.
Modelling relationship between variables.

What is a random variable?: What is the regression line equation?
A variable that takes numerical values d: y = a + bx.
Estimating within range of data.
Estimating outside range of data.
Measure of joint variability of two variables.

Events where P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B).
Events that cannot happen together.
Formula to update probabilities using new evidence.
Long-run average value of a random variable.
Measure of asymmetry of a distribution.
Tail extends to the right.
Range of values likely to contain a population parameter.

What is a random variable?: What affects width of confidence interval?
A variable that takes numerical values d: Sample size, variability, confidence level.
Estimator whose expected value equals true parameter.
Standard deviation of sampling distribution.

Future probability independent of past (Poisson and geometric).
